examples.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm
examples.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation $e^{x+1}=2^x\cdot 5?$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+1} & ={2}^{x}\cdot 5 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x+1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x}\cdot 5)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+1 =\ln \left(2^{x}\cdot 5\right)
$$

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x+1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-1 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-1 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-1}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{8}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{8}^{1-x} & ={3}^{x/2} \\ {log}_{8}⁡({8}^{1-x}) & ={log}_{8}⁡({3}^{x/2})\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
1-x={log}_{8}⁡({3}^{x/2})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
1-x=\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-x & =\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3 \\ 1 & =x+\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3 \\ x+\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3 & =1 \\ 2x+x{log}_{8}⁡3 & =2 \\ x(2+{log}_{8}⁡3) & =2 \\ x & =\frac{2}{2+{log}_{8}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
{log}_{8}⁡(3)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}≈0.528\,321.
$$

Finally,  we can approximate $x$ as 

$$
x≈\frac{2}{2+0.528\,321}≈0.791,
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
